title: Committee of Supply – Head L (Ministry of Sustainability and the Environment)
what_it_is: Committee of Supply – Head L (Ministry of Sustainability and the Environment)

sections.label: Food safety and security bills
sections.summary: Passing the Food Safety and Security Bill and Good Samaritan Food Donation Bill improved food security, water and food supply, and tackled food waste.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: With the recent passing of the 574 pages Food Safety and Security Bill, we have also improved food security in Singapore and ensured a safer supply of fresh water and food.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: With the passing of the Good Samaritan Food Donation Bill, we have ensured that we have done more to tackle food waste.

sections.label: Protection from second-hand smoke
sections.summary: The speaker hopes policies and legislation will change in 2025 to protect people from second-hand smoke in their own homes.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: People depend on us to protect them from second-hand smoke.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: I hope that in 2025, we will finally change our policies and legislation to protect people from second-hand smoke in their own homes.

sections.label: Climate resilience and urban planning
sections.summary: The passage asks how the Ministry will work with business and industry on climate resilience goals and integrate strategies into urban planning.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Razwana Begum Abdul Rahim (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: In this context, how does the Ministry plan to work with business and industry to align their practices with climate resilience goals, and what support is available to help them transition?

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Razwana Begum Abdul Rahim (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: What strategies are the Ministry implementing to enhance the city's resilience to climate change and how are these strategies being integrated into urban planning and development?

sections.label: Scaling up green investments
sections.summary: The Singapore Green Plan has set a foundation, but investments must be scaled up in hydrogen energy, sustainable aviation fuel and carbon capture.

sentences.speaker: Mr Don Wee (Chua Chu Kang)
sentences.text: The Singapore Green Plan has set a strong foundation, but we need to scale-up investments in emerging fields, like hydrogen energy, sustainable aviation fuel and carbon capture technologies.

sections.label: Carbon tax and SME support
sections.summary: The passage suggests exploring differentiated carbon pricing and recommends a Green Transition Fund for SMEs to support transition without compromising growth.

sentences.speaker: Mr Don Wee (Chua Chu Kang)
sentences.text: While Singapore's carbon tax is set to rise, we should explore differentiated pricing to incentivise cleaner energy adoption while ensuring businesses remain competitive.

sentences.speaker: Mr Don Wee (Chua Chu Kang)
sentences.text: Singapore's businesses, especially the small and medium enterprises (SMEs), need support to transition without compromising economic growth.

sentences.speaker: Mr Don Wee (Chua Chu Kang)
sentences.text: I recommend a Green Transition Fund for SMEs.

sections.label: Accelerating coastal protection projects
sections.summary: Projects like the Long Island plan and coastal protection measures must be accelerated with greater private sector participation.

sentences.speaker: Mr Don Wee (Chua Chu Kang)
sentences.text: Projects like the "Long Island" plan and coastal protection measures must be accelerated, with greater private sector participation.

sections.label: Glass facades and air conditioning
sections.summary: Occupants rely on heavy air conditioning, so the speaker suggests building regulations to reduce glass facades in new buildings.

sentences.speaker: Mr Don Wee (Chua Chu Kang)
sentences.text: As a result, occupants rely on heavy usage of air conditioning, which consumes a lot of energy and contributes even more to global warming.

sentences.speaker: Mr Don Wee (Chua Chu Kang)
sentences.text: I suggest that we consider introducing building regulations to reduce the number of glass facades for new buildings.

sections.label: Air conditioning and building emissions
sections.summary: Air conditioning is about 24% of an average household's electricity use, and buildings and homes are Singapore's second-largest carbon emitter at 19%.

sentences.speaker: Ms Poh Li San (Sembawang)
sentences.text: Air conditioning alone accounts for about 24% of an average household's electricity consumption.

sentences.speaker: Ms Poh Li San (Sembawang)
sentences.text: Together, buildings and homes are the second-largest contributor of carbon emissions in Singapore at 19%, of which a significant portion is from air conditioning.

sections.label: Singapore carbon tax rates
sections.summary: Singapore's carbon tax has been raised to $25 per tonne and will rise to $45 per tonne in 2026 and 2027.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gan Thiam Poh (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: Singapore's carbon tax has been increased to $25 per tonne.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gan Thiam Poh (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: It will rise to $45 per tonne in 2026 and 2027.

sections.label: Household recycling survey results
sections.summary: NEA's 2023 survey on household recycling showed 72% of households recycle, compared with 64% in 2021.

sentences.speaker: Dr Lim Wee Kiak
sentences.text: NEA's 2023 survey on household recycling, showed 72% of households recycle compared to 64% in 2021.

sections.label: Recycling contamination and bin collection
sections.summary: Contamination stands at 40%, and the passage details recycling bin sizes and collection frequencies for HDB estates and landed properties.

sentences.speaker: Mr Eric Chua (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: In fact, contamination rate stands at 40%, significantly diminishing the effectiveness of our recycling system.

sentences.speaker: Mr Eric Chua (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: In HDB estates, 660-litre bins are used; one bin to each block.

sentences.speaker: Mr Eric Chua (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: Collections take place at least three times a week.

sentences.speaker: Mr Eric Chua (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: Larger 1,800-litre or 2,200-litre side-loader bins are also deployed but collections only happen once a week.

sentences.speaker: Mr Eric Chua (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: For landed properties, each house is provided with a recycling bin, typically ranging from 180 to 240 litres, with weekly collection services.

sections.label: Bukit Timah First Diversion Canal
sections.summary: The Bukit Timah First Diversion Canal was completed in 2019 after seven years and $300 million, and can take 30% more rainwater.

sentences.speaker: Dr Lim Wee Kiak
sentences.text: Chairman, driving along Bukit Timah Road during rainy season was once the bane of motorists, not to mention residents living in the low-lying areas.

sentences.speaker: Dr Lim Wee Kiak
sentences.text: Then, in 2019, with some fanfare, the Bukit Timah First Diversion Canal was completed after seven years and $300 million spent.

sentences.speaker: Dr Lim Wee Kiak
sentences.text: The 3.2-kilometre canal could take 30% more rainwater than previously.

sections.label: Flood risk scores for properties
sections.summary: The passage asks whether MSE can give flood risk scores to properties in Singapore.

sentences.speaker: Dr Lim Wee Kiak
sentences.text: Can MSE give flood risk scores to properties in Singapore?

sections.label: SFA investigation into premises disamenities
sections.summary: SFA investigated reported disamenities and advised the operator to mitigate noise and heat emissions from food preparation.

sentences.speaker: Mr Muhamad Faisal Bin Abdul Manap (Aljunied)
sentences.text: A recent update from SFA dated 27 February 2025 stated that SFA, in collaboration with relevant agencies, had conducted a thorough investigation into the reported disamenities at the mentioned premises.

sentences.speaker: Mr Muhamad Faisal Bin Abdul Manap (Aljunied)
sentences.text: SFA had advised the operator to implement necessary measures to mitigate resultant noise and heat emissions from their food preparation activities.

sections.label: 30-by-30 grants for high-tech solutions
sections.summary: Grants under the 30-by-30 vision mainly focus on high-tech solutions, leaving a gap in support for low-tech sustainable farming.

sentences.speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Hougang)
sentences.text: Currently, grants under the 30-by-30 vision predominantly focus on high-tech solutions, leaving a gap in support for low-tech sustainable farming practices.

sections.label: Singapore Aquaculture Plan initiatives and sites
sections.summary: The Singapore Aquaculture Plan was launched in November 2024, and the passage asks for details and site exploration updates.

sentences.speaker: Ms Nadia Ahmad Samdin
sentences.text: To uplift the local aquaculture sector, the Singapore Aquaculture Plan was launched in November 2024.

sentences.speaker: Ms Nadia Ahmad Samdin
sentences.text: Can the Ministry provide more details on the initiatives announced in the Singapore Aquaculture Plan, including an update on the exploration of potential sites in the Southern Waters for further studies on integrating closed containment aquaculture systems with open net cage systems for a new hybrid model for fish farming?

sections.label: Funding criteria and commercialisation challenges
sections.summary: Application criteria and evaluation processes make funding access challenging for private enterprises, especially at commercialisation, and partnering public sector performers complicates licensing.

sentences.speaker: Miss Rachel Ong (West Coast)
sentences.text: From a broader perspective, the application criteria and evaluation processes can make it challenging for private enterprises to access funding, especially at the critical stage of commercialisation.

sentences.speaker: Miss Rachel Ong (West Coast)
sentences.text: Additionally, private enterprises are often required to partner public sector performers, leading to complex licensing negotiation that can hinder technology adoption and commercialisation.

sections.label: Wet market stall closures and long-term plans
sections.summary: Wet market stall-owners cited high COE prices for commercial vehicles as a reason to fold, and the passage asks about long-term plans.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Over the last few years, wet market stall-owners have cited very high Certificate of Entitlement (COE) prices for commercial vehicles as another reason to fold up their businesses.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
sentences.text: What is the Ministry's long-term plan for wet markets in smaller and localised neighbourhoods which do not command the footfall they once did, and for wet markets where stalls have seen poor take-ups over the last few years?

sections.label: Hawker centre upgrade plans
sections.summary: Asks whether the Ministry has plans to upgrade or rebuild any hawker centres.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gan Thiam Poh
sentences.text: Would the Ministry share whether there are any plans to upgrade or rebuild any of our hawker centres?

sections.label: NEA hawker competitiveness plans
sections.summary: Asks what NEA's plans are to help hawkers and stores stay competitive.

sentences.speaker: Ms Hany Soh (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
sentences.text: What are NEA's plans to help hawkers and stores stay competitive?

sections.label: Sustaining hawker trade legacies
sections.summary: Asks for an update on efforts to celebrate and sustain the hawker trade and carry on legacies of retiring hawkers.

sentences.speaker: Ms Nadia Ahmad Samdin
sentences.text: Could the Ministry provide an update on its efforts to celebrate and sustain the hawker trade while carrying on the legacies of hawkers approaching retirement, given the lack of successors entering the trade?

sections.label: Two-shift stallholder proposal
sections.summary: Suggests MSE consider a policy allowing two sets of stallholders to operate the same stall in a two-shift system.

sentences.speaker: Mr Eric Chua
sentences.text: To optimise stall utilisation and address this challenge, may I suggest that MSE consider the implementation of a new policy that would allow for two different sets of stallholders to operate the same stall, in accordance with a two-shift system.

sections.label: Joint tenancy and nominee concerns
sections.summary: Asks the reasons hawkers do not readily embrace joint tenancy or nominee models and what NEA or MSE can do.

sentences.speaker: Mr Eric Chua
sentences.text: Under today's provisions, hawkers can appoint a joint operator or a nominee.

sentences.speaker: Mr Eric Chua
sentences.text: Could the Ministry share more from its engagement with hawkers the general reasons for not readily embracing the joint tenancy or nominee model, and what the NEA or MSE might be able to do to address these concerns?

sections.label: Technology support for hawkers
sections.summary: Hopes the Ministry strengthens support for hawkers in technology adoption to preserve hawker culture.

sentences.speaker: Mr Eric Chua
sentences.text: Technology can reduce the physical strain on senior hawkers, allowing them to focus on quality control.

sentences.speaker: Mr Eric Chua
sentences.text: Fancy a plate of Hokkien mee that is 20% spicy, 50% moist, 30% "wok hei", just 3% oily, for Healthier SG's sake?

sentences.speaker: Mr Eric Chua
sentences.text: I therefore hope the Ministry can strengthen support for our hawkers in technology adoption, and in so doing, preserve our much beloved hawker culture for many more generations to come.

sections.label: Public toilet survey scope
sections.summary: A survey covered 2,602 toilets in 1,428 spots and interviewed 4,905 people about public toilet conditions.

sentences.speaker: Ms Hany Soh
sentences.text: The survey looked at 2,602 toilets in 1,428 spots, across coffee shops, hawker centres, MRT stations and shopping malls, and interviewed 4,905 people, including 510 employees, and 4,395 customers about the sentiment on the public toilets conditions.

sections.label: Second-hand smoke deaths
sections.summary: About one death every other day in Singapore is attributable to second-hand smoke, based on the Global Burden of Disease 2019 study.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang
sentences.text: Based on the Global Burden of Disease 2019 study shared by the Ministry of Health (MOH), about one death every other day in Singapore is attributable to second-hand smoke.

sections.label: Public Toilets Task Force
sections.summary: A Public Toilets Task Force was set up in 2024 to study and recommend solutions for poorly performing public toilets.

sentences.speaker: Ms Poh Li San
sentences.text: A Public Toilets Task Force was set up in 2024 to study and recommend solutions to improve the cleanliness of poorly performing public toilets.

sections.label: Toilet Improvement Programme sign-up
sections.summary: The question asks how the Ministry will get owners and operators to sign up for the Toilet Improvement Programme.

sentences.speaker: Ms Poh Li San
sentences.text: How will the Ministry get their owners and operators to sign up for the Toilet Improvement Programme, which provides up to 90% co-funding to improve their toilet designs, install sanitary fittings or adopt technology to facilitate cleaning and maintenance?

sections.label: Dengue risk reduction results
sections.summary: Initial results show residents in sites where the scheme launched are about 75% less likely to be infected with dengue.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gan Thiam Poh
sentences.text: The initial results from the multi-site field study show that residents living in these sites where the scheme had been launched are about 75% less likely to be infected with dengue.

sections.label: NEA project outcomes
sections.summary: NEA reported Aedes mosquito population drops of up to 80% to 90% and a 75% decrease in dengue risk at study locations.

sentences.speaker: Mr Eric Chua
sentences.text: To be sure, the NEA has reported laudable outcomes from the project thus far, Aedes mosquito population at study locations has dropped by up to 80% to 90% and findings from a multi-site field study revealed a 75% decrease in risks of contracting dengue.

sentences.speaker: Mr Eric Chua
sentences.text: Residents in nearby areas have also been found to have a 45% lower risk of contracting dengue than those in areas without releases, indicating that the advantages go beyond immediate zones.

sections.label: Rats chewing car wires
sections.summary: In severe cases, rats have chewed through car wires, causing vehicle damage and thousands of dollars in repair costs.

sentences.speaker: Mr Eric Chua
sentences.text: In a few particularly severe cases, rats have chewed through car wires, causing significant damage to vehicles, resulting in damages amounting to thousands of dollars in repair costs.

sections.label: Smart traps and biological controls
sections.summary: The speaker appeals to MSE to assess Singapore's rat situation and review helping Town Councils defray costs of innovative pest-control solutions.

sentences.speaker: Mr Eric Chua
sentences.text: These modern techniques can possibly include the use of smart traps and biological controls, which have been proven to be more environmentally sustainable and effective as well.

sentences.speaker: Mr Eric Chua
sentences.text: I therefore would like to appeal to the MSE to provide their assessment on the rat situation in Singapore and to review the possibility of assisting Town Councils defray costs associated with implementing the more innovative, albeit costlier pest-control solutions.

sections.label: Technology for ministry productivity
sections.summary: The question asks how the Ministry plans to use social media, mobile apps, AI, IT, technology and automation to improve productivity.

sentences.speaker: Ms Poh Li San
sentences.text: How does the Ministry plan to leverage social media and mobile apps, AI, information technology (IT), technology and automation in its work to improve its productivity?

sections.label: Indoor air-conditioning at 25°C
sections.summary: A major step is to keep indoor air-conditioned spaces at 25°C or higher.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
sentences.text: A major step is to keep indoor air-conditioned spaces at 25°C or higher.

sections.label: Weather Science Research Programme
sections.summary: A $25 million Weather Science Research Programme will be launched to enhance Singapore's ability to understand and predict tropical urban weather, including extreme weather from climate change.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
sentences.text: Climate change poses a serious and considerable threat to Singapore.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
sentences.text: We will launch a $25 million Weather Science Research Programme to enhance Singapore's ability to understand and predict our tropical urban weather, including extreme weather arising from climate change.

sections.label: Reduction in flood-prone areas
sections.summary: Flood-prone areas have been reduced from around 3,200 hectares in the 1970s to less than 25 hectares today, a 99% reduction.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
sentences.text: Over the years, we have reduced flood-prone areas from around 3,200 hectares in the 1970s to less than 25 hectares today – and that is a 99% reduction.

sections.label: Drainage upgrading projects
sections.summary: Infrastructure will be upgraded to enhance flood resilience, with six more drainage upgrading projects expected this year.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
sentences.text: As such, we will upgrade our infrastructure to enhance our flood resilience.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
sentences.text: We can expect six more drainage upgrading projects this year.

sections.label: Flood alert dissemination
sections.summary: PUB uses the myENV app, social media, radio and traditional media for flood updates, with ERP 2.0 flood alerts planned by mid-2025.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
sentences.text: To update Singaporeans on potential flooding, PUB leverages the myENV mobile app, social media, radio broadcast and traditional media outlets to disseminate timely updates.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
sentences.text: There are also plans to enable the ERP 2.0 on-board units in our vehicles to display flood alerts by mid-2025.

sections.label: Coastal protection studies
sections.summary: Studies for Jurong Island, City-East Coast including Long Island, and the northwest coast from Tuas to Woodlands are on track.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
sentences.text: The studies for Jurong Island, City-East Coast, including "Long Island", as well as the northwest coast from Tuas to Woodlands are on track.

sections.label: Coastal and Flood Protection Fund
sections.summary: The Government plans to use annual Budget funds, the Coastal and Flood Protection Fund with a $5 billion top-up, and borrowing.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
sentences.text: The Government plans to use funds from our annual Budget, the Coastal and Flood Protection Fund, to which the Minister for Finance has announced a $5 billion fund top-up, and through borrowing.

sections.label: Coastal Protection Bill
sections.summary: Coastal protection legislation will set stakeholder responsibilities, safeguard land and ensure standards, with a Bill tabled in second half of 2025.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
sentences.text: We are preparing a coastal protection legislation to set out the responsibilities of relevant stakeholders, safeguard land for coastal protection measures and ensure that coastal protection standards are met.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
sentences.text: We will consult stakeholders and table a Coastal Protection Bill in the second half of 2025.

sections.label: Cool coatings on HDB estates
sections.summary: HDB will work with Town Councils to apply cool coatings to all existing HDB estates island-wide by 2030.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
sentences.text: HDB will work closely with the Town Councils to apply cool coatings to all existing HDB estates island-wide by 2030.

sections.label: Hawker Centres Upgrading Programme 2.0
sections.summary: Up to $1 billion will be allocated to upgrade old hawker centres and build new ones over 20 to 30 years under HUP 2.0.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
sentences.text: The Minister for Finance has announced that we will allocate up to $1 billion to upgrade old hawker centres and build new ones.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
sentences.text: We will do these progressively over the next 20 to 30 years, to serve the changing needs of Singaporeans.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
sentences.text: Under a new Hawker Centres Upgrading Programme 2.0 (HUP 2.0), existing hawker centres will be transformed.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
sentences.text: (In Mandarin):   The Hawker Centres Upgrading Programme 2.0 aims to create a more conducive dining and working environment for patrons and hawkers respectively.

sections.label: Rebuilding Hawker Centres in Mature Estates
sections.summary: Some hawker centres in mature housing estates may undergo more extensive rebuilding works.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
sentences.text: Some hawker centres located in mature housing estates may undergo more extensive rebuilding works.

sections.label: Net-Zero Emissions by 2045
sections.summary: The Government has committed to achieve net-zero emissions around 2045, five years ahead of the national target.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
sentences.text: The Government has committed to achieve net-zero emissions around 2045, five years ahead of our national target.

sections.label: Energy Efficiency Fund for Public Buildings
sections.summary: From this year, the Government will set aside around $300 million for an Energy Efficiency Fund for public sector buildings.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
sentences.text: To bolster our efforts, the Government will, from this year, set aside around $300 million for an Energy Efficiency Fund for public sector buildings.

sections.label: Carbon Capture Pilot and Green Tenders
sections.summary: A pilot project by 2026 will validate carbon capture technologies, and from FY2024 up to 5% of tender evaluation criteria cover environmental sustainability.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
sentences.text: A pilot project will be launched by 2026 to validate the carbon capture technologies, such as amine-based absorption for our WtE plants and to inform our next steps.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
sentences.text: To this end, we announced last year that we would refine our environmental sustainability evaluation criteria for large construction and information and communications technology (ICT) hardware tenders.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
sentences.text: I am pleased to share that from FY2024, up to 5% of tender evaluation criteria have been set aside for environmental sustainability considerations.

sections.label: Energy Efficiency Grant Applications Approved
sections.summary: Since introducing the EEG in September 2022, the Government has approved nearly 11,000 applications from over 4,000 businesses.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
sentences.text: Since introducing the EEG in September 2022, the Government has approved nearly 11,000 applications from over 4,000 businesses.

sections.label: Industrial chilled water efficiency standards
sections.summary: From April 2026, MEES for water-cooled chilled water systems in new industrial facilities will be raised to BCA's commercial building standards, saving $63,000 and above annually.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
sentences.text: From April 2026, we will raise the MEES for water-cooled chilled water systems dedicated for space cooling in new industrial facilities to BCA's standards for space cooling in new commercial buildings under the Code for Environmental Sustainability (ES) of Buildings Edition 4.0.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
sentences.text: With the revised energy efficiency standards, each new industrial facility can expect annual energy savings of $63,000 and above over the 15-year lifespan of chilled water systems.

sections.label: HDB Climate Vouchers claimed
sections.summary: As of 31 January 2025, around 80% of eligible HDB households, about 850,000, have claimed their Climate Vouchers.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
sentences.text: As of 31 January 2025, around 80% of eligible HDB households, that is, around 850,000 households, have claimed their Climate Vouchers.

sections.label: Additional Climate Vouchers announced
sections.summary: The Minister for Finance announced the Government will provide an additional $100 of Climate Vouchers to eligible households, on top of the existing $300.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
sentences.text: To encourage greater involvement in climate action, the Minister for Finance announced in his Budget Statement that the Government will provide an additional $100 of Climate Vouchers to eligible households, on top of the existing $300.

sections.label: CFHP expansion household coverage
sections.summary: The expansion will benefit around 250,000 more households, on top of the 1.1 million HDB households already covered under the enhanced CFHP.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
sentences.text: The expansion will benefit around 250,000 more households, on top of the 1.1 million HDB households that are already covered under the enhanced CFHP.

sections.label: Sustainable e-commerce packaging guidelines
sections.summary: The AfA has developed Guidelines on Sustainable E-commerce Packaging to guide companies on sustainable packaging practices, given the sector's continued growth.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
sentences.text: Given the continued growth of this sector, I am pleased to announce that the AfA has developed the Guidelines on Sustainable E-commerce Packaging to guide companies on sustainable packaging practices.

sections.label: Company packaging reduction examples
sections.summary: Watsons Singapore saved up to 10% in packaging procurement costs, and Sealed Air found material in plastic and paper mailers could be reduced by 30% to 50%.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
sentences.text: For example, Watsons Singapore reduced its use of bubble wrap by repurposing shredded used cardboard boxes as filler material, saving up to 10% in overall packaging procurement costs.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
sentences.text: Another example is Sealed Air, who found that with more direct deliveries, the amount of material used in its plastic and paper mailers could be reduced by 30% to 50%.

sections.label: Singapore water demand growth
sections.summary: Water demand is about 440 million gallons a day and is expected to almost double by 2065.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
sentences.text: Our water demand is about 440 million gallons a day today and is expected to almost double by 2065.

sections.label: DTSS freeing up land
sections.summary: The DTSS will free up 150 hectares of land by phasing out intermediate pumping stations and conventional water reclamation plants.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
sentences.text: When completed, the DTSS will free up 150 hectares of land for other purposes by phasing out intermediate pumping stations and conventional water reclamation plants.

sections.label: Singapore food import dependence
sections.summary: Singapore imports over 90% of its food and will not be spared from global food supply disruptions.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
sentences.text: As a country that imports over 90% of our food, Singapore will not be spared from global food supply disruptions.

sections.label: Singapore food import sources
sections.summary: Singapore imports from 187 countries, up from just 140 around two decades back.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
sentences.text: Today, we import from 187 countries, up from just 140 around two decades back.

sections.label: SFA food accreditation streamlining
sections.summary: Since December 2024, SFA has accredited at a broader food category level instead of by food products.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
sentences.text: Since December 2024, SFA has streamlined this process, in line with the work of the Inter-Ministerial Committee on Pro-Enterprise Rules Review, by accrediting at a broader food category level instead of by food products.

sections.label: Maintaining food stocks
sections.summary: Maintaining adequate food stocks helps tide over supply disruptions, though long-term storage of perishable essentials is challenging.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
sentences.text: One complementary strategy is to maintain adequate food stocks to tide over supply disruptions, as seen during the COVID-19 pandemic.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
sentences.text: For perishable essentials like fibre, long-term storage is challenging, involving inventory and logistics costs.

sections.label: NEA littering enforcement and CCTV
sections.summary: NEA increased littering enforcement in 2024 with about 130 blitzes and up to 1,000 CCTV deployments a year.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
sentences.text: In 2024, NEA increased littering enforcement, conducting about 130 blitzes, a six-fold increase from 2023.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
sentences.text: NEA’s camera surveillance capabilities were also strengthened, allowing up to 1,000 CCTV deployments a year, compared to 250 in 2023.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
sentences.text: Last year, CCTVs were deployed 300 times at 13 identified littering hotspots, enhancing operational effectiveness leading to a 36% reduction in litter count between May and December 2024.

sections.label: Rat-related enforcement actions
sections.summary: In 2024, NEA and SFA took more than 1,000 enforcement actions against premises owners or occupiers for rat-related lapses.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
sentences.text: In 2024, intensified enforcements by NEA and SFA saw more than 1,000 enforcement actions, almost twice the number in 2023, taken against premises owners or occupiers for rat-related lapses.

sections.label: Project Wolbachia household coverage
sections.summary: By the end of 2026, 800,000 households, about 50% of all Singaporean households, will benefit from Project Wolbachia.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
sentences.text: By the end of 2026, 800,000 households, or about 50% of all Singaporean households, will benefit from Project Wolbachia.

sections.label: Coffee shop toilet renovation funding
sections.summary: Coffee shop operators can apply to NEA for up to 95% funding of toilet renovation costs and two-year deep cleaning contract costs.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
sentences.text: Coffee shop operators can apply to NEA for funding of up to 95% of their toilet renovation costs, capped at $50,000 per coffee shop.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
sentences.text: They can also apply for up to 95% funding of their two-year deep cleaning contract cost, capped at $25,000 per coffee shop.

sections.label: Public toilet cleanliness inspections
sections.summary: In 2024, NEA and SFA carried out close to 19,000 public toilet cleanliness inspections and about 1,300 enforcement actions.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
sentences.text: In 2024, NEA and SFA stepped up inspections on public toilet cleanliness.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
sentences.text: Close to 19,000 inspections were carried out, with about 1,300 enforcement actions taken against premises owners and managers.

sections.label: Coffee shop toilet grants funding
sections.summary: MSE will allocate $10 million to launch the Coffee Shop Toilet Renovation Grant and Coffee Shop Toilet Deep Cleaning Grant.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
sentences.text: MSE will allocate $10 million to launch the Coffee Shop Toilet Renovation Grant and Coffee Shop Toilet Deep Cleaning Grant.

sections.label: NEA video analytics enforcement
sections.summary: NEA will use more video analytics and AI for surveillance and enforcement, with data identifying hotspots needing greater intervention.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
sentences.text: NEA will embrace greater use of video analytics and AI to enhance surveillance and enforcement capabilities, with data used to identify hotspots that require greater intervention.

sections.label: PUB drainage inlet AI inspection
sections.summary: Since February 2024, PUB has used an AI-enabled video analytics solution to inspect drainage inlets along 7,000 kilometres of roadside drains.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
sentences.text: Since February 2024, PUB has implemented an AI-enabled video analytics solution to inspect drainage inlets along 7,000 kilometres of roadside drains.

sections.label: SFA second-generation mobile lab
sections.summary: SFA is developing a second-generation mobile lab that can handle substantially higher testing volume with faster results.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
sentences.text: SFA is now developing a second-generation mobile lab that can handle substantially higher testing volume with faster results.

sections.label: SG Eco Fund Sprout grant raised
sections.summary: The maximum grant for the SG Eco Fund's Sprout category was raised from $8,000 to $30,000 for successful applications received this year.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
sentences.text: To catalyse more community-led projects, we have raised the maximum grant for the SG Eco Fund's Sprout category, which is the entry tier, from $8,000 to $30,000 for all successful applications received this year.

sections.label: Panel recommendations on recycling rates
sections.summary: The Panel has submitted its recommendations to address low domestic recycling rates.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
sentences.text: The Panel has since submitted its recommendations to address low domestic recycling rates.

sections.label: No technology for home smoking ban
sections.summary: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary said there is no current technology to catch someone smoking at home, so a ban cannot be legislated.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang
sentences.text: And I am sure he expects me to clarify further.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang
sentences.text: But I think the Senior Parliamentary Secretary mentioned that there is no current technology to catch someone smoking at home and, so, because of that we cannot legislate a ban.

sections.label: NEA advisories on smoking
sections.summary: NEA issues advisories urging residents not to smoke at windows and balconies, which often fails, and CDRT also fails for lack of evidence.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang
sentences.text: So, NEA will issue advisories urging that resident to not smoke at the windows and balconies.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang
sentences.text: That often fails, and we try CDRT, and that fails because they cannot gather the evidence.

sections.label: Smoking disamenity at home
sections.summary: The disamenity of smoking at home is recognised, and action will be taken once the right surveillance technology is found.

sentences.speaker: Mr Baey Yam Keng
sentences.text: But I assure Mr Ng and all those concerned about smoking at home causing disamenity, which I also receive similar feedback from my residents, that we recognise the disamenity.

sentences.speaker: Mr Baey Yam Keng
sentences.text: And as soon as we are able to find a way with the right technology to be able to do surveillance and detect smoking at private spaces, at windows and balconies, we will do something.

sections.label: Free drinking water at F&B outlets
sections.summary: There are no plans to require F&B outlets to provide free or low-cost drinking water.

sentences.speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
sentences.text: With regard to the F&B outlets, we do not have any plans to go and require them to provide free drinking water, for instance, or at low cost.

sections.label: Water cost for F&B owners
sections.summary: Water is a valuable resource and is not free because F&B owners have to pay for the water.

sentences.speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
sentences.text: The other thing is, actually, water is a valuable resource and even though water can be taken freely from the tap, it is not free, because the F&B owners have to pay for the water.

sections.label: Prioritising centres for HUP 2.0
sections.summary: Many factors go into prioritising a centre for HUP 2.0, including how critical the centre is and residents' needs.

sentences.speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
sentences.text: Chairman, with regard to the first question from Member Ms Hany Soh, there are many factors that will go into the consideration on prioritising the centre for HUP 2.0.

sentences.speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
sentences.text: First, we will look at the centre, how important or how critical is the centre requiring major transformations.

sentences.speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
sentences.text: Second, we have to look at the needs of the residents in that area.

sections.label: Grants focus on coffee shop toilets
sections.summary: Grants focus on coffee shop toilets because surveys over many years show they consistently fare lowest in cleanliness.

sentences.speaker: Mr Baey Yam Keng
sentences.text: As for the grants to extend beyond coffee shops, the reason why we are focusing on coffee shop toilets now is because, based on surveys over many years, coffee shop toilets have fared consistently at the lowest level of cleanliness.

sections.label: Bakery noise heat smell HDB
sections.summary: Member asks whether SFA receives feedback on bakery noise, heat and smell in HDB blocks and whether regulations exist.

sentences.speaker: Mr Muhamad Faisal Bin Abdul Manap
sentences.text: What happened was that there is this issue that has been going on for about 10 years where the bakery located in the same block, a four-storey HDB block, has been emanating noise, heat and pungent smell.

sentences.speaker: Mr Muhamad Faisal Bin Abdul Manap
sentences.text: And then they did mention that they are working with other relevant agencies to look into the matter.

sentences.speaker: Mr Muhamad Faisal Bin Abdul Manap
sentences.text: But my question is basically whether SFA has received similar feedback on such issues and how pieces of feedback are being received in a year, and also whether there is any requirement for bakeries that operate in an HDB residential block in managing the noise and heat level resulting from their daily operation.

sentences.speaker: Mr Muhamad Faisal Bin Abdul Manap
sentences.text: Is there any kind of regulation or requirement imposed by SFA?

sections.label: SFA ventilation noise regulations
sections.summary: Speaker says he would consider the Member's suggestions of having more regulations to regulate businesses on ventilation and noise.

sentences.speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
sentences.text: On the feedback about SFA imposing regulations on ventilation as well as on noise, I would very much consider the Member's suggestions of perhaps having more regulations to regulate the businesses.
